scientificReview.reason: Both languages distinguish cornea from sclera, iris pigmentation from dye, lens structure from a membrane, gel-like vitreous, retinal photoreceptors from optic-nerve branches, and neural signaling. Textual correspondences 1 through 10 remain intact. The pupil range is approximate and condition/person dependent. This does not establish the unseen modern anatomy figure.

Near-axis/paraxial equivalent converging thin-lens analysis is explicitly a simplification of the multisurface eye. Image distance is approximately fixed, not an exact invariant of a real changing eye. Inverted real retinal imaging and the non-flat, living-retina qualification are retained in both languages.

Muscle/fiber-mediated curvature change replaces literal whole-body lens compression. Closer viewing increases curvature and reduces equivalent focal length. Visual angle and the source arcminute reference are retained without a guaranteed one-cell resolution rule. The near point is an actual conditional focusing limit; the ideal infinite far point is bound to relaxed accommodation without refractive error.

The retained 25 cm value is a conventional elementary-optics reference, not a universal near point or comfort distance. Myopic and hyperopic distance statements remain source-bound but conditional. No d0 equation, measured near point or new numerical recommendation is introduced.

Both languages preserve eye rotation and binocular retinal-image differences as distance/depth cues. Neither asserts universal growth of left-right muscle-tension difference or uses muscle tension as a direct distance ruler.

Relaxed myopic focus before the retina, finite far point, diverging correction and backward extensions through A are retained. Hyperopic behind-retina convergence is hypothetical onward propagation in the relaxed geometric-optics model, not a claim that the retina transmits the rays. Compensation depends on available accommodation. Converging correction, reduced near-ray divergence and the farther virtual image retain the source construction under its stated conditions, not a universal result for every converging lens. This is not diagnosis or a prescription.

staticEvidence.method: Read-only Node JSON/hash/equality assertions plus independent semantic reading. No lesson-tool import or execution. Existing native prose-flow JSON and successful receipts were read, not regenerated.
semanticSectionTransitions: Accommodation/near point to conventional viewing distance

findings.title: Explain the eye-specific mechanism in concrete steps

locations.sentence: Second complete sentence in both locales
locations.enExcerpt: ciliary muscle activity changes the pull on the lens through the suspensory fibers, allowing greater lens curvature and a shorter equivalent focal length
locations.reason: This introduces the muscle, connecting fibers, pulling force, curvature and focal-length result in one compressed sentence. Neither version explains the new eye-specific muscle/fiber names in ordinary words, and 'changes the pull' leaves a child to infer what actually happens. This is not a false scientific claim, but does not provide an independently readable causal explanation for the declared child learner.

locations.sentence: Second complete sentence in both locales, and the concluding reduced-demand sentence
locations.enExcerpt: its optical power must match the eye's refractive state and the assumed accommodation state
locations.reason: The explanation compresses lens matching, the selected focusing state and retinal imaging into abstract state/demand language. The conclusion 'without the original greater demand' points back to the same abstraction instead of stating plainly what effort is reduced. Chinese carries the same problem. Retaining scientific conditions is necessary; expressing them this abstractly is not.

findings.affectedOnlyChange: Revise only the identified mechanism/correction sentences in /prose/4/text and /prose/14/text in both locales. Give the muscle/fibers a brief plain-language gloss and describe near focusing as reduced fiber pull allowing the lens to become rounder. Explain lens matching in terms of where light focuses and whether the focusing muscles are relaxed; say plainly that less near-focusing effort is needed. Preserve the existing model qualifications, all source concepts, snapshots, refs, formula tokens and figure occurrence order. This is a local readability repair, not permission to rewrite the lesson.
findings.recheckScope: Only changed sentences/paragraphs, bilingual meaning, preservation and anchors whose text actually changes; all unaffected scientific and structural conclusions remain reusable.
